slides.0.points.0.text: Covering geography, climate, grape varieties and classification

slides.0.points.1.text: Think carefully about each question; you can go back and review at any time
slides.1.question: Which Portuguese region is the world's first wine region under continuous government regulation (1756)?
slides.1.explanation: In 1756 Portugal's Marquis of Pombal formally demarcated the Douro/Porto region and placed it under continuous regulation, making it the world's first regulated wine region.
slides.2.question: What does "Verde" in "Vinho Verde" mean?
slides.2.options.0: The wine is green in colour
slides.2.explanation: "Verde" means young and fresh, indicating that Vinho Verde is a young, crisp style of wine, regardless of colour.
slides.3.question: What is the Alvarinho variety called in Spain?
slides.3.explanation: Alvarinho (Portugal) and Albariño (Spain) are the same variety, best known in Rías Baixas and Vinho Verde.
slides.4.question: What is the main soil type of the Douro Valley?
slides.4.explanation: Schist (Xisto) is the main soil of the Douro Valley. It retains heat well and roots can dig deep for water, forming the foundation of Port quality.
slides.5.question: Which EU tier is equivalent to Portugal's DOC tier?
slides.5.explanation: Portugal's DOC (Denominação de Origem Controlada) is equivalent to the EU's DOP (Protected Designation of Origin).
slides.6.question: The Baga variety is known for high acidity and high tannin. In which DOC is it mainly planted?
slides.6.explanation: Baga is the soul variety of Bairrada DOC, known for very high acidity and tannin; with age it can develop complex leather and mineral aromas.
slides.7.question: How many sub-regions does Alentejo have?
slides.7.explanation: Alentejo DOC has 8 sub-regions: Portalegre · Borba · Redondo · Reguengos · Vidigueira · Évora · Granja-Amareleja · Moura.
slides.8.message: 🎉 Congratulations on completing all of Level 1! You have built a complete foundation in Portuguese wine.
slides.8.keyPoints.0: Geography: 14 official regions from Minho in the north to Algarve in the south, plus two Atlantic island regions
slides.8.keyPoints.3: Varieties: Touriga Nacional (red) and Alvarinho (white) are the most representative
slides.8.keyPoints.4: Regions: Douro (Port) · Vinho Verde (fresh whites) · Alentejo (rich reds)
